text:
Devin Cooley was never drafted. He got to the NHL as a free agent, by way of 26 AHL games with the Milwaukee Admirals, and on Saturday night he was the reason the Flames won their third straight. Calgary beat Detroit 4-1 while being chased most of the night, and Cooley stopped 28 of 29 shots.

By our numbers, the Red Wings played the better game. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances, favored DET 2.78 to 1.49, and they out-attempted the Flames 57 to 38. In the simulated replays of every shot, Detroit wins about 74 percent of the time. Cooley saved roughly 1.8 goals more than the chances he faced should have allowed. At the other end, John Gibson gave up about 2.5 more than his workload deserved.

The game turned in the second period. Andrew Copp tied it at 1-1 early, then the Flames scored three times in 10 minutes. Zayne Parekh's power-play goal came on a 3 percent chance. Ryan Strome added one at even strength, and Matvei Gridin, the 2024 first-round pick, scored on another power play with 1:30 left in the period. Calgary went 2 for 2 on the man advantage, Detroit 0 for 2. Joel Farabee had a goal and two assists. Calgary has now won three in a row, while Detroit leaves with a loss it had little reason to expect.
